text:
The biggest thing in Detroit isn't on the ice. Dylan Larkin, the captain, has refused to play until the Red Wings trade him, and he is suspended, listed through Dec 20. Thursday the team took down a banner with his face on it and put up one of Emmitt Finnie. The Hockey Writers now count Larkin, Simon Edvinsson and Rochette on Detroit's exit list. That is the backdrop for a team that has lost four of five and won the chance battle in none of them, averaging 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) over that stretch.

The hockey problems are real too. Andrew Copp has taken Larkin's spot beside Lucas Raymond and Viktor Arvidsson, up to 19:20 a night, and Finnie has moved onto the top power play. Raymond has goals in three straight. Arvidsson and Alex DeBrincat are the frustrating part: Arvidsson has nine games without a goal on 2.9 expected, DeBrincat three points in ten on 8.4 expected. Our projected starter is John Gibson, who is .862 this season and .851 over his last five, though Daniil Tarasov has started recent games and the headlines say the staff likes what he's given them.

The Islanders arrive with points in six straight and a player who has become the show. Matthew Schaefer, last year's first overall pick, has 14 points in his last ten, including a hat trick against Columbus on Tuesday, and our numbers say he earned it. Simon Holmstrom has points in six straight. The honest caveat: New York's results are ahead of its chances, plus 8 in goals on minus 9.8 expected, propped up by Ilya Sorokin (11.1 goals saved above expected). Ryan Pulock's latest injury has no update yet, per Pete DeBoer.

Casey Cizikas plays his 1,000th NHL game, a long road for a fourth-round pick who became the heartbeat of a checking line. Our playoff race has New York at 37% and Detroit at 14%, and you'd feel that number in Detroit.
headline: Larkin's absence hangs over a sinking Detroit
